title: Local root tensors determine maps from positive powers
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a scheme $X$, and $d\in\mathbf N$. Let $N$ be a sheaf of modules over the completed integral coefficient ring of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Two module-sheaf morphisms from the positive completed integral root power of exponent $d$ to $N$ are equal if they agree, on every pro-etale object $U$, on every ordered pure-root generator formed from a completed scalar $a$ and a $d$-tuple of compatible roots, as defined in [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. At $d=0$ the generator is $a$ in the scalar unit; at $d=1$ it is $a\cdot(1\otimes x)$; at higher degrees it is the ordered tensor of these root factors, with the scalar in the first factor. No invertibility hypothesis on $\ell$ on $X$ is required for this extensionality assertion about the constructed tensors.

source.place: Integral twist and Powers and duals paragraphs; local pure-tensor uniqueness in the orientation coefficient conventions

proof.text: For exponent zero the generator is an arbitrary scalar section, so sectionwise equality is immediate. For exponent one forget to additive sheaves and apply the scalar-extension sheafification adjunction. Before sheafification the tensor is generated by b tensor x. The completed-action equation identifies this with the completed image of b times (one tensor x), so equality on the specified generators gives equality on every tensor.

For exponent n+2 apply the tensor-sheafification adjunction, reducing to pure tensors v tensor w. Apply the induction hypothesis in the first variable and the first-line argument in the second variable. Restrictions of the root generators are the same generators of the restricted scalars and roots, so these tests may be performed after restriction to each slice. The ordered root generator is precisely the tensor of the generator at n+1 and the last root at scalar one. Tensor induction gives equality before sheafification, hence equality of sheaf maps. No basis or nonempty-scheme hypothesis is used.

proof_origin.place: Integral twist and Powers and duals: make the normalized module comparison and the generator uniqueness explicit.

theorem sfPositiveRootGenerator_hom_ext
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : Scheme.{u}) (d : ℕ)
    {N : integralTowerModules l E X}
    {f g : FrobeniusCoefficientTwists.positiveLine l E X d ⟶ N}
    (h : ∀ (U : X.ProEtᵒᵖ)
      (a : (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E X).obj.obj U)
      (x : Fin d → (purTwistZlOne X l).obj.obj U),
      f.val.app U (FrobeniusCoefficientTwists.generator l E X U a d x) =
        g.val.app U (FrobeniusCoefficientTwists.generator l E X U a d x)) : f = g
